steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Primary: contemporary to event (documents, artefacts, oral testimony); Secondary: later analysis by historians

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: OPVL: Origin (who, when, where), Purpose (why created), Value (what it reveals), Limitation (what it omits/distorts)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Reliability: accuracy, bias, typicality; Utility: usefulness for specific enquiry

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Historiography: Whig (progress), Marxist (class struggle), Revisionist (challenge orthodoxy), Postmodern (multiple truths)

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: Evaluate the utility of a 1917 Bolshevik poster for a historian studying propaganda in the Russian Revolution --- Solution: Origin: Bolshevik party, 1917. Purpose: mobilise support, demonise opponents. Value: reveals Bolshevik messaging, visual rhetoric, target audience (workers/soldiers). Limitation: one-sided, omit failures, not objective. Utility: high for studying propaganda techniques, low for factual accuracy of events

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Apply OPVL to a diary entry from WWI | Compare two historians' views on the causes of the English Civil War | Explain the difference between reliability and utility
